text: Writing clean code is a skill that saves time and frustration for everyone involved. The most important goal is to write readable code, meaning that another programmer can understand your logic without a struggle. Start with clear naming conventions; a variable called `userAge` is far better than `x`, and a function named `calculateTotal` immediately explains its purpose. Instead of writing one long block of logic, break your work into small, focused functions which each do a single task. This approach greatly improves maintainability, allowing you to fix bugs or add new features quickly. In short, always write code as if the person who will maintain it is a violent person who knows where you live.
